requirements.title: Source-cited OctopusG specification pack
acceptance: docs/00–10, ADR-0001…0005, REQUIREMENTS.yaml, TRACEABILITY.md and SESSION_BRIEF.md exist.
Every requirement and capability cites at least one resolvable source in docs/sources/.
The five planes are defined, including the meaning of Data Plane and State Store.

requirements.title: Specification validator and generated traceability
acceptance: `npm run validate:spec` checks YAML syntax, duplicate IDs, required fields, enums, dependency existence, cycles and milestone order, source anchors, internal Markdown links, capability coverage, milestone coverage, requirement IDs mentioned in docs, and staleness of generated sections.
`npm run spec:write` regenerates TRACEABILITY.md, the capability table and the SESSION_BRIEF status block.
The validator uses only dependencies already in package-lock.json.

requirements.title: AI session guardrails in the repository
acceptance: CLAUDE.md states identity, authoritative files, rules and prohibited actions, and imports SESSION_BRIEF.md.
.claude/settings.json denies push, remote changes, provider CLIs, network tools, dependency installs and secret-file reads.
.claude/settings.local.json is git-ignored.

requirements.title: Work-package evidence records
acceptance: Each finished work package has docs/evidence/WP-nn.md listing commands run, results, requirement status changes and open questions.
validate:spec fails if a requirement is IMPLEMENTED or VERIFIED without an evidence file naming it.

requirements.title: Reconcile README and v0.1 documents with repository state
acceptance: README.md names OctopusG, states the pinned registry version and row count, and has no broken links.
docs/DATA_MODEL.md registry-version statements match the importer.

requirements.title: Governance archive of Gate artifacts
acceptance: docs/archive/ holds (or records the location and SHA-256 of) PROJECT_REGISTRY_v1.6.yaml, GATE_3B_COMPLETION.md, PRODUCT_BACKLOG.md, GATE_2C_2D_3_3B_ACTION_LOG.md and the v0.1 Git bundle.
Recorded hashes match S1; the historical HTML map is marked non-authoritative.
PRODUCT_BACKLOG.md items are checked against the capability atlas and any missing idea is added as CONCEPT.

requirements.title: Fail-closed registry ingestion (v0.1 baseline)
acceptance: Importer rejects wrong filename, version, row count, duplicate IDs, unknown categories and duplicate YAML keys.
Snapshot is deterministic and preserves every registry field.

requirements.title: Single registry lock manifest
acceptance: data/registry.lock.json holds filename, registry_version, sha256 and project_row_count.
Importer, schema checks, unit tests and browser tests read expected values from the lock instead of hard-coded literals.
A hash or count mismatch still fails the build with a message naming the file.

requirements.title: Ingest PROJECT_REGISTRY v1.6
acceptance: data/PROJECT_REGISTRY_v1.6.yaml is present and its SHA-256 equals 494bd33e056350c15524a87fe73e9adc02bb6e8bfcd79ea4e801ec58f5b43286.
The lock points to v1.6; all views render the v1.6 row count; v1.5.1 stays in data/ as history.

requirements.title: Typed resource catalog derived from the registry
acceptance: Repository, checkout, domain, deployment and document resources are derived from existing registry fields with the source path of each.
No resource is fetched or guessed; missing values stay unknown.
Each product lists its resources in the evidence drawer.

requirements.title: Declared legal-entity ownership records
acceptance: Legal entities are declared data; a product without a declared owner entity shows "undeclared", never a default.

requirements.title: v0.1 views preserved
acceptance: Portfolio, Matrix, Ecosystem, Deployment drift, Approval queue, Timeline, KPIs and Connectors render with no browser errors or external requests.

requirements.title: OctopusG naming in the interface
acceptance: Header, title and README show "OctopusG — AgoraXAI Portfolio Operating System".
Schema codename and localStorage key are unchanged so saved simulation state still loads.

requirements.title: Truth and freshness badges
acceptance: Catalog and matrix show the truth kind and observed_at for observed values; stale values are visibly marked.
Keyboard and screen-reader users get the same information as text.

requirements.title: Devices screen (declared)
acceptance: Lists declared devices with trust zone, capabilities and prohibited operations.
The company laptop appears as BROWSER_ONLY / UNMANAGED / NO_LOCAL_ACCESS.

requirements.title: Requirements and capability status view
acceptance: A read-only view shows capability statuses and requirement counts by milestone and status, built from REQUIREMENTS.yaml at build time.

requirements.title: Owner cockpit summary
acceptance: One screen answers: what happened, which product, which account, did automation respond, what needs approval, what executed, did it succeed, how the map changed.

requirements.title: OctopusG brand mark and visual identity
acceptance: The owner-supplied mark is preserved byte for byte as the master in assets/brand/, and its hash, dimensions, format, byte size, transparency and provenance are recorded and checked by a test.
Served derivatives are crops and resizes of the master only, carry no metadata, and are smaller than it.
The compact symbol and the favicon carry no wordmark; the full lockup is shown only where its wordmark and the approved tagline remain legible.
The visible word OctopusG stays real text, every brand image is local and every decorative image has empty alternative text.
No semantic colour, stored key, schema constant or export shape changes.

requirements.title: Declared ecosystem graph (v0.1 baseline)
acceptance: Only explicit parent fields create ownership edges; Atlas is never owned by Artemis.

requirements.title: Typed relationship graph including resources
acceptance: Graph nodes include products and derived resources; every edge has a type from docs/02, a truth kind and a source.
Ownership edges still come only from declared fields.

requirements.title: Generated lane-layout map
acceptance: Node positions are computed from lanes; no coordinates are stored in data.
A toggle colors nodes by exactly one of lifecycle, risk band or truth kind.
Declared, observed and derived edges are visually distinct and also distinguishable without color.

requirements.title: Map presets: portfolio and repository views
acceptance: Portfolio view (products and relationships) and repository view (products, repositories, checkouts) are selectable and filter the same graph.

requirements.title: Deployment, domain, device, account and risk views
acceptance: Additional presets render from connector-imported resources and show freshness.

requirements.title: Map regenerates after connection changes
acceptance: Connecting or revoking a connection changes graph resources on the next build; revoked resources are marked disconnected, not removed.

requirements.title: Owner-run local Git observer
acceptance: `npm run observe` reads only paths in config/observe.allowlist.json.
It runs only rev-parse, status --porcelain (counts only) and remote (names only) with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0 and a timeout.
Output records ok, missing, not_a_repo or error per path with observed_at and expires_at; no filenames, file contents or remote URLs are stored.
The checkout is byte-for-byte unchanged after a run (including .git/index).

requirements.title: Declared-versus-observed drift
acceptance: Drift view compares declared path, branch and remote presence with the latest observation and shows match, differs, stale or unknown.
A failed or stale observation is never shown as a match.

requirements.title: Recorded deployment drift (v0.1 baseline)
acceptance: Compares recorded source and production SHAs; unknown stays unknown; no ancestry is inferred.

requirements.title: Connector health and data freshness monitoring
acceptance: Each connection shows last successful sync, error state and freshness; expired data raises observation.stale.

requirements.title: Business KPIs from sales and leads
acceptance: KPIs have written definitions, owners and windows; simulated data never feeds them.

requirements.title: External observability integration (logs, incidents)
acceptance: Evaluate Sentry, Better Stack or Grafana as observe-only sources before any build decision.

requirements.title: Read-only DayOS monitor (source, checkout, deployment reference)
acceptance: The DayOS source repository, checkout and branch are derived from two named registry rows (the DayOS git_state and the one other product that checks out the same branch), never assumed; with no unique match the monitor shows unknown.

DayOS is added to config/observe.allowlist.json as the only change to it, for read-only Git observation only; the allowlist content is pinned by a test and the observer's five read-only Git commands are unchanged. DayOS is observed within the Artemis Omni repository; this establishes no ownership, no dedicated DayOS repository, no deployment or production status and no authority to modify Artemis Omni.

The DayOS monitor shows repository, checkout, branch, HEAD, working tree, remote, deployment reference and the declared Supabase inventory, each with a state (observed, declared, derived, unknown, not-collected, stale, error or blocked), its truth kind, its provenance and, where observed, its timestamp and expiry.

No row claims health. No observation reads not-collected, a failed one error, an expired one stale; live deployment and live Supabase state are blocked while their connections are at level 0. No Supabase or provider access exists.
Open actions are the existing safe set — a derived repository link and a copy-only folder path; no website is offered because none is declared.

DayOS appears in the resource graph as a derived source-repository edge and in the drift table against the hosted checkout; a derived edge exists only between existing named registry rows with explicit source evidence, and simulated inbox events are labelled and never affect a state.
This requirement does not authorize any connector, credential, deployment or mutation.
The monitor module is pure (no network, filesystem, process or clock) and writes nothing; the inspected checkout is byte-for-byte unchanged after an observer run.

requirements.title: One-command registry repoint
acceptance: One owner-run command verifies a new registry file, rewrites data/registry.lock.json, runs npm run validate and reports the result without committing.

requirements.title: Approval outcomes written to a governance record
acceptance: A completed, authenticated approval appends its outcome to a governance record inside the repository; simulated approvals never do.

requirements.title: Five-kind truth model
acceptance: declared, observed, derived, approved and executed are representable alongside unknown and blocked.
Existing v0.1 evidence values keep their meaning; v0.1 tests still pass unchanged.

requirements.title: Observation store with freshness
acceptance: Observations carry observed_at, collected_at, expires_at and status; the build reads work/observations/latest.json when present.
Absent observations render as "not collected", errors as errors, expired values as stale.
Secret-shaped values are rejected before persistence.

requirements.title: Personal-data retention and redaction policy
acceptance: Before any message content is stored: written retention periods, redaction rules and deletion procedure approved by the owner.

requirements.title: Append-only local state store
acceptance: Events, action requests, approvals and audit entries are appended, exportable and integrity-checked; nothing is edited in place.

requirements.title: Vercel read-only connection
acceptance: Owner can authorize a Vercel account.
Projects and deployments are discovered.
No production mutation is possible.
Imported relationships appear on the system map.
Deployments not created through the Git integration (e.g. CLI deployments from a side branch) are flagged.

requirements.title: Connector contract and definitions
acceptance: Connector definitions follow docs/04 (resources, observations, events, actions, maxLevel, scopes).
A connection can never exceed its connector maxLevel; tests prove it.
The five v0.1 stubs are expressed as definitions and still return blocked.

requirements.title: Connection Center at Level 0
acceptance: Cards show the fields listed in docs/08; owner actions are visible but disabled with the reason.
The lifecycle states are shown; no authorization flow exists; no network request is possible.

requirements.title: Disabled connector stubs stay blocked (v0.1 baseline)
acceptance: All five stubs return blocked observations without network or filesystem access.

requirements.title: GitHub read-only connection
acceptance: Allowlisted repositories report visibility, default branch, branch SHAs and check conclusions.
No contents, workflows, issues or writes.

requirements.title: Approved HTTP route probes
acceptance: Only approved HTTPS routes; bounded redirects, time and size; soft-404 control; no bodies stored.

requirements.title: Safe revoke and disconnect lifecycle
acceptance: Revocation stops events, removes webhooks, revokes the credential, keeps non-sensitive audit, marks resources disconnected and warns about dependent workflows.

requirements.title: Tailscale device inventory (read-only)
acceptance: Enrolled devices and online state are observed with a read-only scoped client; ACL, tag and authorization changes stay manual.
Expired or disconnected devices are flagged.

requirements.title: n8n workflow bridge
acceptance: OctopusG can call one inbound n8n webhook for test workflows and receive normalized results; executions are observed.

requirements.title: Gmail watch and drafts
acceptance: One owner-authorized mailbox; new inquiries become events; replies are created as drafts only.

requirements.title: ManyChat observation and campaigns
acceptance: Campaigns, keyword triggers and lead events are observed where the API permits; otherwise an Open in ManyChat link is shown.

requirements.title: Instagram/Facebook via official Meta APIs
acceptance: Professional account only; comment webhooks and permitted private replies; no scraping or cold outreach.

requirements.title: WhatsApp Business Platform
acceptance: Business Platform only; opt-in, templates and conversation windows enforced; no personal WhatsApp.

requirements.title: Squarespace read-only commerce and site events
acceptance: Orders, sales and site events are observed read-only.

requirements.title: Supabase read-only metadata
acceptance: Owner-reviewed, sanitized schema/migration inventory only; no rows, credentials, function bodies or queries.
Before implementation, project identity resolves from authoritative canonical configuration and cross-validates to dayos; otherwise state is blocked.
The initial design allowlist excludes object counts and caps the connector at Level 1 with metadata:read.
G3 remains a separate owner authorization and is not granted by the design package.

requirements.title: Evaluate third-party social and inbox backends
acceptance: Written comparison of respond.io, SleekFlow, Trengo, Sprout Social, Hootsuite, Buffer against OctopusG needs before any integration.

requirements.title: Normalized event envelope
acceptance: Events follow docs/05; simulated events are labelled and excluded from KPIs.
Duplicate deliveries de-duplicate on (connector, provider_event_id).

requirements.title: Simulated inbox from fixtures
acceptance: Inbox renders fixtures/events/*.json with filters for product, connector, severity, requires-decision and status.
Every item is visibly SIMULATED; no personal data appears in fixtures.

requirements.title: Real deployment events in the inbox
acceptance: Vercel deployment created/succeeded/failed appear as observed events with links to the provider.

requirements.title: Local webhook receiver
acceptance: A separately reviewed ADR defines the receiver; signatures are verified; the static app server is unchanged.

requirements.title: Event correlation across channels
acceptance: comment → lead → draft → sent events share a correlation_id and appear as one story.

requirements.title: Declared device registry and trust zones
acceptance: config/devices.json declares the personal Mac, personal Windows laptop (not enrolled) and company laptop (BROWSER_ONLY).
Validation rejects any capability on a company-owned device.

requirements.title: Device online status and project location
acceptance: Map and devices screen show which device holds each checkout and whether it is online.

requirements.title: Local agent enrollment and allowlisted commands
acceptance: Enrollment is owner-initiated and authenticated; only allowlisted, parameter-validated commands run for an approved action ID.

requirements.title: Offline action queue
acceptance: Actions for an offline device wait and are re-validated against current policy before running.

requirements.title: Directory move detection with confirmation
acceptance: A moved checkout is proposed as a registry change; nothing is updated without owner confirmation.

requirements.title: Personal Windows laptop enrollment
acceptance: Windows agent passes the same contract tests as the Mac agent.

requirements.title: Workflow catalog
acceptance: n8n workflows are listed with state and associated products.

requirements.title: Trigger approved test workflows and pause failing ones
acceptance: Only approved test workflows can be triggered; a failing workflow can be paused with an audit record.

requirements.title: Artemis inquiry to Gmail draft pilot
acceptance: Artemis inquiry → inbox → AI-prepared draft → owner approval → sent by owner → lead status updated.

requirements.title: Instagram keyword comment to lead flow
acceptance: Keyword comment → approved private reply → n8n normalization → lead linked to product → Gmail follow-up draft.

requirements.title: WhatsApp Business inquiry and guest flows with human handoff
acceptance: Approved templates only; human handoff for anything sensitive.

requirements.title: AI-drafted workflows for approval
acceptance: AI may propose n8n workflow drafts; publishing needs owner approval.

requirements.title: Approved-template automatic acknowledgments
acceptance: Only named, owner-approved templates for narrow messages (e.g. inquiry acknowledgment) may send at Level 4; pricing, contracts, disputes and personal matters never qualify.

requirements.title: Safe open actions
acceptance: Open website and Open provider are plain links to registry-recorded HTTPS URLs with rel="noopener noreferrer".
Open folder shows the path with a Copy button; `npm run open -- <product-id>` opens only allowlisted paths.
The audit still finds no browser network client.

requirements.title: Action requests with tier and level policy (simulated)
acceptance: A pure policy function decides allow/deny from action tier, connection level, approval and preconditions, with the reason.
T3/T4 requests require all seven fields in docs/06 §3 before they can be approved.
Everything remains labelled simulation.

requirements.title: Approval simulation (v0.1 baseline)
acceptance: Sequential stages, mandatory notes, rollback only after execution, falsified state rejected.

requirements.title: Allowlisted local actions
acceptance: Launch an approved local app and run approved tests on an enrolled device, with evidence.

requirements.title: Guarded preview and deployment promotion
acceptance: Promotion requires a verified preview, explicit approval and a rollback path.

requirements.title: Guarded database migrations
acceptance: Proposed migration, affected objects, backup, dry-run, rollback, approval and evidence are all required.

requirements.title: Critical actions: DNS, secrets, deletion, money
acceptance: Strong confirmation, verified backup and audit; never Level 4.

requirements.title: Real authenticated approvals
acceptance: Authenticated owner identity, per-item scope, evidence references, append-only storage, integrity and revocation.

requirements.title: Loopback-only static server and isolation audit (v0.1 baseline)
acceptance: 127.0.0.1 only, GET/HEAD only, Host check, CSP connect-src none, no browser network client, zero remotes, credential-pattern scan.

requirements.title: Trust zones, tiers and levels as data
acceptance: config/policy.json encodes trust zones, tiers T0–T4 with minimum levels, and the rule that Level 4 never applies to T3/T4.
Tests cover every tier/level combination.

requirements.title: Credential references in macOS Keychain
acceptance: Only collector/executor processes may resolve a credential by a provider reference; values never reach source, configuration, the bundle, UI, logs, events, observations, snapshots, evidence, generated artifacts or canonical records.
CredentialRef and CredentialProvider remain provider-neutral; connectors and business logic do not depend directly on macOS Keychain.
Audit proves no credential value is present in tracked output or work/observations.

requirements.title: Secret containment precondition for connector authorization
acceptance: Connector authorization is refused while unresolved plaintext-secret exposure is recorded, unless the owner records an explicit exception.

requirements.title: Kill switch
acceptance: One control pauses every connection and executor; state is visible on every screen.

requirements.title: Messaging compliance guard
acceptance: Consent, rate limits and messaging windows are enforced before any send; sensitive categories always need human approval.

requirements.title: Cloud control plane security design
acceptance: An ADR covers hosting, authentication, MFA, secrets, agent channel and blast radius before any cloud deployment.

requirements.title: Verified recovery copy of the control-plane repository
acceptance: The owner confirms the location and hash of a current off-machine recovery copy (bundle or private remote) and it is recorded in docs/evidence/WP-13.md.

requirements.title: Continuous integration runs validation and specification checks
acceptance: A GitHub Actions workflow runs npm ci --ignore-scripts, npm run validate and npm run validate:spec on every pull request and every push to the default branch, using only the committed package and lock files.

The workflow is added to .github/workflows/ as a design artifact under ADR-0007 and takes effect only once the repository exists at the one approved origin; it is never enabled against a public or unverified repository.

requirements.title: Protected, non-production preview deployment only
acceptance: A single Vercel project on the $0 tier is linked to the approved-origin private repository and deploys previews only; no production deployment or custom domain is ever created by this requirement.
The strongest protection available on the $0 plan is enabled and independently verified before any preview URL is shared or used.
If protected preview at $0 is not achievable, no deployment is made and the blocker is recorded instead of a workaround.

requirements.title: Read-only registry MCP server for AI sessions
acceptance: Local stdio server exposes read-only tools (get product, list resources, where is checkout, latest observation); no write tools; no network.

requirements.title: Event summaries and suggested reply drafts
acceptance: AI output is always a draft with its inputs cited; never sent automatically.

requirements.title: Diagnostics and recommendations
acceptance: Failed deployments and drift produce cited diagnostic notes labelled derived.

requirements.title: Bounded AI agents
acceptance: Agents act only through ActionRequest → policy → approval; hold no credentials; cannot raise levels.

requirements.title: Evidence-governed multi-model engineering claims
acceptance: Structured claims retain claim identity, object/entity identity, model/provider/version identity, evidence, provenance, assumptions, confidence, uncertainty, disagreement, dissent, counterevidence, verification state, deterministic solver results where applicable, temporal state, human review state and approval state.

No individual AI model, provider or agent is engineering truth or final engineering authority; evidence quality and authoritative observations outrank model consensus, and no majority vote establishes engineering truth.

Material disagreement is explicit and retained without silent averaging, overwriting, hiding or collapse into false certainty; AI synthesis may propose a resolution but has no independent engineering approval authority. Resolution approval requires the owner and/or appropriately authorized human professional according to role, domain and applicable professional responsibility, preserving required licensed professional judgment, original claims, dissent, counterevidence, a traceable rationale and explicit human identity and authority.

Validated deterministic engineering solvers remain authoritative for numerical calculations within their validated scope; LLM numerical assertions cannot silently become validated professional engineering results.

Evidence and authority gates preserve AI proposal, independent challenge/cross-check, evidence support, solver verification where applicable, engineer review where required, owner/authorized-party approval, issuance, construction and physical observation/validation, reconciled with canonical state models; simulated approvals confer no real authority.

Temporal/scenario lineage preserves earlier observations and alternatives; model-reported confidence does not replace canonical derived confidence, and missing evidence or authorization remains unknown or blocked.

requirements.title: Tenancy boundary between the internal group and clients
acceptance: Every legal entity and product carries a tenancy, `internal`, `organization:<id>` or `client:<id>`; missing tenancy shows "undeclared".
An ownership edge whose ends are in different tenancies is rejected at load with the edge and both tenancies named.
Explicit service, client and funding edges (provides_services_to, pays_for_services, client_of, funds) may cross tenancy and never imply ownership or resource access.
Any internal organization roll-up across entities refuses client-tenancy or undeclared-tenancy rows and says why; all-registry inventory counts are labelled as inventory, not ownership totals.

Business ownership and control are distinct from product and asset ownership; S9 declarations are represented without inferring domain, repository, IP, partner equity, payment, nonprofit, tax or accounting facts.
Pınar Evleri is client:pinar-evleri, owned independently by the collectively described cousins; its registry row keeps that client tenancy.
Missing tenancy is undeclared; known-to-unknown ownership fails closed, including legacy platform_parent edges.
Validation can check the pinned importer output without writing a pre-existing snapshot; mismatches still fail closed.

requirements.title: Scoped partner shares with undeclared values
acceptance: A share is scoped to an entity, project or product and names a holder and interest kind with declared provenance; its percentage may be `undeclared`. No unknown partner is invented and contractual/economic interests create no equity edge.
An undeclared percentage is shown as "undeclared" and blocks any attribution that needs it; nothing defaults to 0 or 100.
Declared percentages within one scope that exceed 100 are rejected at load.

requirements.title: Explained variance
acceptance: A field may declare which declared components explain its observed value and a tolerance.
A difference fully explained within tolerance is reported as explained, with each component and its truth state; the weakest component sets confidence.
Any unexplained remainder stays `differs`; stale or missing components yield `unknown`, never explained.

requirements.title: Cost basis and depreciation register
acceptance: A schedule is computed only when every judgement it needs (allocation, life, method, convention, FX policy) is declared; otherwise it is blocked with the missing parameter named.
Output truth is `derived`; no computed figure is ever `observed`.

requirements.title: Dated compliance obligations with verbatim citations
acceptance: Every obligation cites a primary source with a verbatim excerpt and retrieval date; an uncited obligation is rejected.
Computed due dates are `derived`, carry a legal-holiday caveat, and are never shown as verified.
